A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SecureGate work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite reformatting and content relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original inference/extraction attack experiments, baseline comparisons, perplexity measurements, and component analyses on ECHR and Yelp.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds measured inference latency for gated and standalone adapters in Table 4.

M1.justification: The dual adapters, federated optimization, fusion objectives, gating network, and two-pass inference remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2. Appendix D.1 details the previously described hash/PRNG embedding construction without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: ECHR and Yelp, inference/extraction tasks, authorization conditions, and non-IID and multi-adapter scenarios are retained. The added latency evaluation uses existing Llama-1B/ECHR coverage.

E2.justification: The five federated baselines and standalone secure/revealing adapters are retained. The new timing comparison uses the already evaluated standalone adapters without introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Table 4 adds per-pass latency in milliseconds and relative inference overhead, comparing gated and standalone adapters on Llama-1B/ECHR. Existing training settings, data partitions, attack protocols, and metrics are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds a component-cost analysis isolating the extra gating pass against standalone adapter execution. Existing rank, gating-feature, defense, heterogeneity, candidate-pool, and multi-adapter analyses remain; the multi-adapter analysis is relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Client-level variability reporting in the scalability analysis is retained, with no added experimental run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Appendix D.1's seeds concern key construction, not repeated experimental trials.

E6.justification: All eight original tables retain their numerical entries, and Figures 2–7 retain identical plotted content. New Table 4 reports a 197.14 ms gating pass, secure/revealing adapter passes of 1501.71/1463.55 ms, and approximately 1.13× inference cost.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds formal key, seed, and embedding definitions and an entropy/brute-force calculation in Equations (10)–(15), including approximately 119-bit key entropy. Existing optimization equations and threat assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same selective-disclosure contribution and privacy, utility, and efficiency claims, including the headline leakage reductions and 100% routing result. The latency addition supports the existing efficiency claim.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the measured gating cost as modest and predictable and adds specific reasoning about brute-force infeasibility and embedding non-invertibility. Earlier interpretations and limitations concerning latency, memory, key secrecy, and model scope are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly specifies MD5-based seed construction, Gaussian embeddings, and 20-character keys over a 62-symbol alphabet. Table 1 clarifies the ECHR/Llama-1B setting, and a named SecureGate repository pointer replaces the anonymous code link.

R1.justification: V2 adds Akbik et al. (2019) for Flair and Peng et al. (2024) for the extraction discussion, replacing unresolved citations in v1. The related-work argument and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the conclusion, standardizes model names, repairs cross-references, and moves the multi-adapter discussion from Appendix B-C into Section 5.2. Most prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted with different margins, typography, headings, captions, and float placement. Figure 1 is visually revised, Figure 6's panels become larger and vertically stacked, former Table IV becomes full-width main-text Table 3, and timing Table 4 is added.

improvement.justification: Table 4 quantifies the gating-latency cost that v1 only discussed qualitatively, while Appendix D.1 makes key generation more reproducible. These provide limited transparency gains. Timing repetitions and uncertainty remain unspecified, and the new security discussion incorrectly describes entropy growth as exponential despite Equation (10)'s linear dependence on key length.
